title: Galaxy clusters leave a rotational fingerprint on the cosmic microwave background
topic: Galaxies & Galactic Evolution / Cosmology & Early Universe
verifiedFacts: The analysis combined Planck microwave intensity and polarization data with Sloan Digital Sky Survey member-galaxy redshifts.
The final sample contained 25 nearby, massive, X-ray cross-matched galaxy clusters.
The oriented stack showed a rotation-aligned dipole at 3.6 sigma, exceeding 99.98 percent of 30,000 random stacks.
The authors use rotational kSZ broadly: the measured internal gas motions can include coherent rotation and merger-driven flows.
The signal amplitude and shape are qualitatively consistent with hydrodynamical simulations.
